theory.intro: Real shapes like tents, sails and bridge trusses are rarely one labelled right-angled triangle. Find the right-angled triangles inside the shape, solve the one that has enough information, then carry that result into the next.
facts: Solve one triangle at a time, choosing the one where two of the three quantities are already known.
A total length, such as a perimeter, a span or a gap, is the **sum or difference** of lengths found separately.
Keep the unrounded value on the calculator between stages and round **once**, at the end, to the accuracy asked for.
If no diagram is given, sketch one: mark the right angle first, then the known lengths and angles.
steps: Identify the right-angled triangles in the figure
Mark the unknown and any side the triangles share
Solve the triangle that has enough information
Carry that result into the second triangle
Answer the question that was asked

development.question_text:
A surveyor stands at a point $A$ on the straight bank of a canal, directly opposite a marker $M$ on the far bank.
She walks $68$ m along the bank to $B$, where the line $BM$ makes an angle of $41^{\circ}$ with the bank.
She then walks a further $25$ m along the bank to $C$.
Draw a diagram, then find the angle that $CM$ makes with the bank, correct to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
Because $M$ is directly opposite $A$, the width $AM$ is perpendicular to the bank, so $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle ACM$ are both right-angled at $A$.
$\tan41^{\circ}=\frac{AM}{68}$
$AM=68\tan41^{\circ}$
$=59.1115\ldots\text{ m}$
$AC=68+25$
$=93\text{ m}$
$\tan\theta=\frac{59.1115\ldots}{93}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{59.1115\ldots}{93}\right)$
$=32.4403\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx32^{\circ}$

\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (P) at (0,0);\coordinate (Q) at (4.87851,0);\coordinate (S) at (1.50176,1.92216);\coordinate (U) at (3.37675,1.92216);\draw (-0.7,0)--(P);\draw (Q)--(5.58,0);\draw[dashed] (P)--(Q);\draw[very thick] (P)--(S) node[midway,above left] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (Q)--(U) node[midway,above right] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (S)--(U) node[midway,above] {$15\text{ m}$};\pic[draw,"$52^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.75cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Q--P--S};\pic[draw,"$52^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.75cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=U--Q--P};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A drawbridge is made of two identical sections, each $x$ m long, hinged at opposite banks of a river.
Lowered, the two sections exactly span the river.
Raised to $52^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, their tips are $15$ m apart.
Find the width of the river, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
Lowered, the sections span the river, so the river is $2x$ m wide.
Raised, each section covers a horizontal distance of $x\cos52^{\circ}$, and what is left over is the gap.
$2x-2x\cos52^{\circ}=15$
$2x(1-\cos52^{\circ})=15$
$2x=\frac{15}{1-\cos52^{\circ}}$
$=39.0280\ldots$
$\approx39.0\text{ m}$

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.6]\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (7.4,0);\coordinate (A) at (2.73043,3.03245);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$7.4\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\pic[draw,"$48^{\circ}$",angle radius=1.2cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=R--L--A};\pic[draw,"$33^{\circ}$",angle radius=1.5cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=A--R--L};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The end wall of a shed is $7.4$ m wide.
Its left rafter rises at $48^{\circ}$ and its right rafter at $33^{\circ}$.
Find the height of the ridge above the wall top, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Dropping the vertical from the ridge makes two right-angled triangles whose bases add to $7.4$ m.
$\tan48^{\circ}=\frac{h}{p}$, so $p=\frac{h}{\tan48^{\circ}}$
$\tan33^{\circ}=\frac{h}{q}$, so $q=\frac{h}{\tan33^{\circ}}$
$\frac{h}{\tan48^{\circ}}+\frac{h}{\tan33^{\circ}}=7.4$
$h\left(\frac{1}{\tan48^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\tan33^{\circ}}\right)=7.4$
$h=\frac{7.4}{2.4402\ldots}$
$=3.0324\ldots$
$\approx3.03\text{ m}$

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (2.7,0);\coordinate (D) at (1.35,0);\coordinate (A) at (1.35,2.16045);\coordinate (S) at (0.56238,0.9);\coordinate (U) at (2.13762,0.9);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$2.7\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\draw[very thick] (S)--(U);\draw[dashed] (D)--(1.35,0.9) node[midway,right] {$0.9\text{ m}$};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The end of an A-frame tent is $2.7$ m wide and its sloping sides make $58^{\circ}$ with the ground.
A horizontal spreader bar is fixed across the tent $0.9$ m above the ground.
Find the length of the spreader bar, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
At each end of the bar, the ground, the sloping side and the $0.9$ m height form a small right-angled triangle.
$\tan58^{\circ}=\frac{0.9}{d}$
$d=\frac{0.9}{\tan58^{\circ}}$
$=0.5623\ldots\text{ m}$
The bar is what is left of the $2.7$ m width after removing $d$ at each end.
Bar $=2.7-2\times0.5623\ldots$
$=1.5752\ldots$
$\approx1.58\text{ m}$
